# 4 eras of NLP

## Era 1: Symbolic era {.center}

*1950s–1970s*

**Complex, hard-coded rules written by linguists**

Alan Turing's ["Computing Machinery and Intelligence"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computing_Machinery_and_Intelligence) (1950)

IBM's Russian to English translations (1954)

First rule-based chatbot: MIT's [ELIZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA) (1964—1967)

## Era 2: Lexical search {.center}

*1980s–1990s*

**Statistical methods**

Algorithms learn patterns & probabilities from data (large corpora)

## Era 3: Dense retrieval {.center}

*2000s–2010s*

**Machine learning & early deep learning models**

Vector embeddings, e.g. [Word2Vec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word2Vec) (2013)

Mathematical representation of words based on their semantic meanings & contextual relationships

[Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recurrent_neural_network) such as [Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_short-term_memory) networks for speech recognition & translation

## Era 4: LLMs {.center}

*2017–present*

**Transformer based large language models**

Self-attention mechanism

Massive scaling

Generative AI

[BERT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BERT_(language_model)), [GPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Products_and_applications_of_OpenAI#Text_generation), [Gemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_(language_model)), [Claude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_(AI)), etc.

# The question <br>

:::{.question}

If LLMs can do everything, are task-specific methods dead?

Let's find out with one test case

:::

## Benchmark: BEIR/SciFact {.center}

[SciFact](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.14974) [@wadden2020factfictionverifyingscientific] dataset: a benchmark for scientific claim verification (2020) \
Part of the [BEIR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08663) [@thakur2021beir] standard suite of information retrieval benchmarks

- [5,183 scientific abstracts]{.emph}
- [1,409 scientific claims]{.emph}
- [Expert annotators' ground truth]{.emph}

## Get the data {.center}

```{.bash}
curl -L -o scifact.zip \
  https://public.ukp.informatik.tu-darmstadt.de/thakur/BEIR/datasets/scifact.zip
```

:::{.notenoit}

Alternative methods to get the data:

- from the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/allenai/scifact)
- from [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/scifact):

```{.python}
from datasets import load_dataset
dataset = load_dataset("allenai/scifact")
```

:::

## Structure of the data {.center}

[scifact.zip]{.codelike} unzips to a [scifact]{.codelike} dir with:

[corpus.jsonl]{.codelike}: a corpus of research abstracts \
  ➔ `id`, `title`,` text` (abstract of scientific paper)

[queries.jsonl]{.codelike}: scientific claims to be verified against the corpus \
  ➔ `id`, `text` (claim), `label` (`contradict` / `support`)

[qrels]{.codelike} dir with [train.tsv]{.codelike} & [test.tsv]{.codelike}: relevance judgment for training & testing \
  ➔ `corpus-id`, `query-id`, `score`

## Methods {.center}

::::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}

**Lexical ranking algorithm** \
Sparse keyword search

- [BM25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okapi_BM25)

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}

**Dense retrieval** \
Semantic vectors via embeddings

- [all-minilm](https://ollama.com/library/all-minilm) (23M)
- [nomic-embed-text](https://ollama.com/library/nomic-embed-text) (137M)
- [mxbai-embed-large](https://ollama.com/library/mxbai-embed-large) (335M)

:::

::::

**Reciprocal Rank Fusion** \
Hybrid keyword + embeddings

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}

**LLMs** \
Reranking the shortlist

- [llama3.2 3b](https://ollama.com/library/llama3.2:3b)
- [llama3.1:8b](https://ollama.com/library/llama3.1:8b)

:::

::::

## Metric: nDCG@10 {.center}

[Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discounted_cumulative_gain) at rank 10 is a standard ranking quality metric in information retrieval, search engines & recommendation systems

Measures how well a system places the most relevant items within the first 10 results

```{.python}
def ndcg_at_k(ranked, qrels, k=10):
    dcg = sum(qrels.get(d, 0) / np.log2(r + 2)
              for r, d in enumerate(ranked[:k]))
    ideal = sorted(qrels.values(), reverse=True)[:k]
    idcg = sum(g / np.log2(r + 2) for r, g in enumerate(ideal))
    return dcg / idcg if idcg else 0.0
```

## Metric: nDCG@10 {.center}

Expected scores:

- 0.45 – 0.65: Typical range for standard e-commerce or keyword search engines
- 0.70 – 0.80: Strong search quality
- 0.80+: Exceptional performance, usually powered by advanced AI re-rankers or semantic/hybrid search

## Hardware: one small GPU {.center}

For this test, the hardware used was a laptop with: \
8 cores, 16 threads, 30 GiB of RAM, and a **small 6GiB GPU**

## Load packages {.center}

```{.python}
import json
import numpy as np

# https://github.com/ollama/ollama-python
import ollama

# https://github.com/dorianbrown/rank_bm25
from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi
```

## Load corpus {.center}

```{.python}
corpus = {}  # doc id -> {"title": ..., "text": ...}

with open("scifact" / "corpus.jsonl", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        doc = json.loads(line)
        corpus[doc["_id"]] = {
            "title": doc.get("title") or "",
            "text": doc["text"],
        }
```

## Load queries {.center}

```{.python}
queries = {}  # query id -> text

with open("scifact" / "queries.jsonl", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        q = json.loads(line)
        queries[q["_id"]] = q["text"]
```

## Load relevance judgments {.center}

```{.python}
qrels = {}  # query id -> {doc id: relevance}

with open("scifact" / "qrels" / "test.tsv", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    next(f)
    for line in f:
        qid, did, score = line.split("\t")
        qrels.setdefault(qid, {})[did.strip()] = int(score)
```

# Lexical ranking algorithm

## BM25 {.center}

A [bag-of-words](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bag-of-words_model) retrieval function ranks documents by how relevant they are to a search query. It uses literal keyword matches (1994)

Improved version of [term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF-IDF)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tf–idf) with length normalization

No training, CPU-based, still widely used (e.g. [Elasticsearch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elasticsearch))

:::{.note}

Fails on [vocabulary mismatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocabulary_mismatch) & paraphrase

Example: "heart attack" does not match "myocardial infarction"

:::

## Code {.center}

```{.python}
def tokenize(text):
    """Crude but sufficient: lowercase alphanumeric tokens."""
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())

# Build the index
bm25 = BM25Okapi([tokenize(full_text[d]) for d in docs])

# Score every document
scores = bm25.get_scores(tokenize(query))

# Sort
ranking = [docs[i] for i in np.argsort(-scores)]
```

## Result {.center}

```
BM25  nDCG@10 0.652  (15.0 ms/query)
```

:::{.emph}

0.652 with zero training, one second of indexing & 15 ms per query

:::

A very serious baseline on this dataset

# Dense retrieval

## The idea {.center}

A trained [embedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embedding_(machine_learning)) model maps texts to vectors based on meaning

- Index: embed every abstract once
- Search: embed the query, rank by [cosine similarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosine_similarity)
- Solves vocabulary mismatch: "heart attack" & "myocardial infarction" have close vectors

:::{.note}

Dense retrieval does not scan text; it compares coordinates. That is why it needs an index of embeddings

:::

## 3 model sizes {.center}

| Model             | Params | Year | Disk   |
|-------------------|--------|------|--------|
| all-minilm        | 23M    | 2020 | 45 MB  |
| nomic-embed-text  | 137M   | 2024 | 274 MB |
| mxbai-embed-large | 335M   | 2024 | 669 MB |

Pulled by [ollama](https://ollama.com):

```{.bash}
ollama pull all-minilm nomic-embed-text mxbai-embed-large
```

Served locally:

```{.bash}
ollama serve
```

## Embedding the corpus {.center}

```{.python}
def embed(texts, model, batch=64):
    out = []
    for i in range(0, len(texts), batch):
        out.extend(ollama.embed(model=model,
                                input=texts[i:i+batch])["embeddings"])
    emb = np.asarray(out, dtype=np.float32)
    # L2-normalization
    emb /= np.linalg.norm(emb, axis=1, keepdims=True)  # unit vectors
    return emb

doc_emb = embed([full_text[d] for d in docs], model)
```

L2-normalization makes every later dot product a cosine similarity

:::{.note}

On the laptop GPU, indexing 5,183 abstracts took 150 s with the largest model

:::

## Searching {.center}

```{.python}
q = np.asarray(
    ollama.embed(model=model, input=[query])["embeddings"][0],
    dtype=np.float32,
)
# L2-normalization
q /= np.linalg.norm(q)

ranking = [docs[i] for i in np.argsort(-(doc_emb @ q))]
```

One matrix-vector product against the whole corpus: [20 milliseconds]{.emph}

:::{.inlinenote}

Each model gets its recommended query format \
Abstracts are truncated at each model's own context limit

:::

## Results {.center}

```
all-minilm         nDCG@10 0.648  (20.1 ms/query)
nomic-embed-text   nDCG@10 0.703  (18.1 ms/query)
mxbai-embed-large  nDCG@10 0.741  (22.3 ms/query)
```

The 2020 miniature model ties BM25

The modern models do better

Bigger embedding model → better rankings at [the same milliseconds per query]{.emph}

# Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)

## The idea {.center}

Fuse two rankings by rank position, no score calibration needed [@10.1145/1571941.1572114]

```{.python}
RRF_K = 60  # classic constant (Cormack et al. 2009)

def rrf(rankings):
    fused = {}
    for qid in eval_qids:
        scores = {}
        for ranking in rankings.values():
            for rank, d in enumerate(ranking[qid]):
                scores[d] = scores.get(d, 0.0) + 1.0 / (RRF_K + rank)
        fused[qid] = sorted(scores, key=scores.get, reverse=True)
    return fused
```

## Results {.center}

```
RRF (nomic + BM25):   0.702 -> 0.706   # helped a little
RRF (mxbai + BM25):   0.741 -> 0.731   # hurt
```

Whether or not a hybrid method helps depends

- With a mediocre embedder, fusion buys back what each method misses
- Once one signal is much stronger, [fusing drags it down]{.emph}

:::{.note}

Hybrid search is a patch for weak retrieval

:::

# LLMs

## The constraint {.center}

A generative model [cannot scan 5,183 abstracts]{.emph}: \
it has no index & reads tokens one prompt at a time

The standard pattern is [retrieve-then-rerank]{.emph}:

- Retrieve a shortlist: top-10 BM25 or top-10 dense (≤ 20 documents)
- Ask an LLM to reorder the shortlist
- One LLM call per query: [extremely high compute demand]{.emph}

## A naive prompt {.center}

```{.python}
resp = ollama.chat(
    model=model,
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a search reranker."},
        {"role": "user", "content":
            f"Query: {query}\n\nDocuments:\n{listing}\n\n"
            "Rank the documents by relevance to the query. "
            "Reply with the document numbers, most relevant first."},
    ],
    format=RERANK_FORMAT,   # JSON schema: {"ranking": [integers]}
    options={"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 200, "num_ctx": 16384},
)
```

:::{.inlinenote}

Full abstracts (median ~360 tokens), so the prompt needs a 16k-token context window

:::

## What came back {.center}

Several replies per run could not be parsed:

```
query: 'The combination of H3K4me3 and H3K79me2 is found in
        quiescent hair follicle stem cells.'
response: '{ "ranking": [1, 3, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18,
            19, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 5, 7, 2, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5,
error: Expecting value: line 32 column 3 (char 168)
```

:::{.note}

The model counts & loops over numbers until the generation cap cuts the JSON mid-list: [9 of 50 replies unparseable]{.emph}

:::

## The fallback hid the failures {.center}

The reply is text: code has to turn it into a ranking

```{.python}
try:
    nums = json.loads(resp["message"]["content"])["ranking"]
    ranked = [shortlist[n - 1] for n in nums
              if 1 <= n <= len(shortlist)]
except (ValueError, KeyError, IndexError):
    ranked = shortlist   # fallback: keep the retriever order
```

:::{.note}

Every unparseable reply silently keeps the retriever's ranking: [the measured score was partly the retriever's work, not the LLM's]{.emph}

:::

## A tighter prompt {.center}

State the number of documents, the valid range & the reply length

```{.python}
resp = ollama.chat(
    model=model,
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a search reranker."},
        {"role": "user", "content":
            f"Query: {query}\n\nDocuments:\n{listing}\n\n"
            f"There are {len(shortlist)} documents, numbered "
            f"1 to {len(shortlist)}. Reply with the 10 most relevant "
            "document numbers, most relevant first."},
    ],
    format=RERANK_FORMAT,   # JSON schema: {"ranking": [integers]}
    options={"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 200, "num_ctx": 16384},
)
```

:::{.inlinenote}

Zero unparseable replies from both models

:::

## What the 3B model replied {.center}

Real reply to the tighter prompt, for a query whose gold document sat at position 1 of the shortlist:

```
shortlist: 20 docs | gold document at position 1

llama3.2 replied: { "ranking": [21, 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12] }
```

:::{.note}

21 does not even exist — the model counts down from N: [the tighter prompt fixed the format, not the judgment]{.emph}

:::

## Results {.center}

```
llama3.2 3B   listwise rerank   nDCG@10 0.295  (5.1 s/query)
llama3.1:8B   listwise rerank   nDCG@10 0.557  (14.4 s/query)
```

:::{.note}

The 8B produces genuine orderings — [both models still damage the 0.693 retrieval they rerank]{.emph}

:::

## Score, do not generate {.center}

The listwise prompt asks the model to [do arithmetic over list positions]{.emph} — exactly what small transformers fumble

Instead: judge one document at a time & read the answer from the model's own distribution

## Score, do not generate {.center}

One small prompt per document — not one giant prompt per query:

```{.python}
resp = ollama.chat(
    model=model,
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a search reranker."},
        {"role": "user", "content":
            f"Claim: {query}\n\nAbstract: {full_text[d]}\n\n"
            "Is this abstract relevant to the claim? "
            "Answer with exactly one word: yes or no."},
    ],
    logprobs=True, top_logprobs=10,
    options={"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 1, "num_ctx": 2048},
)
```

## The score {.center}

```{.python}
lp = {e["token"]: e["logprob"]
      for e in resp["logprobs"][0]["top_logprobs"]}

yes = max(lp[t] for t in ("yes", "Yes", " yes"))
no  = max(lp[t] for t in ("no", "No", " no"))

score = np.exp(yes) / (np.exp(yes) + np.exp(no))  # P(yes)
```

Rank the shortlist by P(yes)

:::{.note}

P(yes) straight from the model's distribution: [no list to count, no text to parse]{.emph}

:::

## Pointwise results {.center}

```
llama3.2 3B   pointwise  nDCG@10 0.668  (3.3 s/query)
llama3.1:8B   pointwise  nDCG@10 0.722  (7.6 s/query)
```

:::{.emph}

The same models, the same 50 queries — the 8B now beats the 0.693 retriever it starts from

:::

## Same 50 queries {.center}

All the LLM methods run on 50 queries; the retrievers re-scored on the same 50:

| Method                        | nDCG@10 | Per query |
|-------------------------------|---------|-----------|
| llama3.1:8B pointwise         | 0.722   | 7.6 s     |
| mxbai-embed-large (retriever) | 0.693   | 22 ms     |
| llama3.2 3B pointwise         | 0.668   | 3.3 s     |
| RRF hybrid (retriever)        | 0.651   | —         |
| BM25 (retriever)              | 0.606   | 15 ms     |
| llama3.1:8B listwise          | 0.557   | 14.4 s    |
| llama3.2 3B listwise          | 0.295   | 5.1 s     |

Asked to generate a ranking, both models [damage the retrieval they start from]{.emph} — scored on their probabilities, the 8B edges past it

# Verdict

## {.center}

| Era | Method                        | nDCG@10 | Per query |
|-----|-------------------------------|---------|-----------|
| 2   | BM25                          | 0.652   | 15 ms     |
| 3   | all-minilm (23M)              | 0.648   | 20 ms     |
| 3   | nomic-embed-text (137M)       | 0.703   | 18 ms     |
| 3   | mxbai-embed-large (335M)      | 0.741   | 22 ms     |
| 2+3 | RRF hybrid                    | 0.731   | —         |
| 4   | llama3.2 3B listwise rerank   | 0.295*  | 5.1 s     |
| 4   | llama3.1:8B listwise rerank   | 0.557*  | 14.4 s    |
| 4   | llama3.2 3B pointwise rerank  | 0.668*  | 3.3 s     |
| 4   | llama3.1:8B pointwise rerank  | 0.722*  | 7.6 s     |

:::{.inlinenote}

*on the 50-query subset. Same benchmark, same hardware: a laptop with a 6 GiB GPU

:::

## The cost of the LLM {.center}

|               | Embedding search | LLM reranking            |
|---------------|------------------|--------------------------|
| Per query     | 22 ms            | 3.3 s (3B) to 7.6 s (8B) |
| Slowdown      | 1×               | [150× to 345×]{.emph}    |
| Model on disk | 669 MB           | 2.0 to 4.9 GB            |

:::{.note}

Best-case columns: the pointwise numbers — the listwise prompts were slower still. And only the 8B pointwise beats the embedder

:::

## Takeaways {.center}

- [Embeddings remain a practical and efficient choice for semantic search]{.emph}, and they scale gracefully: bigger model, better rankings, same milliseconds
- Hybrid fusion patches weak retrieval, but drags down strong retrieval
- A prompted generative model is [not automatically better]{.emph}: asking it to generate a ranking was the worst method
- Used right — scoring with its [probabilities]{.emph} instead of its prose — the 8B LLM beat the retriever it reranked on the same queries, [at 345× the cost]{.emph}

## Reach for the LLM when {.center}

The task is [generative]{.emph}:

- Summarize, answer, explain, discuss...
- Extract claims & entities

:::{.note}

Retrieval and generation are different jobs. Let the embedder retrieve and the LLM do what only an LLM can do — or score with it when ranking quality matters more than speed

:::
